component.name: Blazzing
component.summary: Fast visual IPTV client for Linux
Cliente IPTV visual rápido para Linux

description.p: Blazzing is a native C17/X11 IPTV client focused on a fast, responsive visual interface.
It supports Xtream Codes and M3U playlists, live TV, movies, series, favorites, playback progress, metadata, thumbnails and an embedded mpv player.
Blazzing é um cliente IPTV nativo em C17/X11 focado em uma interface visual rápida e responsiva.
Suporta Xtream Codes e M3U, TV ao vivo, filmes, séries, favoritos, progresso, metadados, miniaturas e player mpv incorporado.
Adds on-demand artwork resolution for visible movie and series cards, backed by the shared Blazzing artwork service and TMDB poster URLs.
Adiciona resolução de capas sob demanda para cards visíveis de filmes e séries, usando o serviço compartilhado de capas do Blazzing e URLs de pôsteres do TMDB.
Fixes the Linux QR pairing caption so the displayed expiration matches the actual 45-second session timeout.
Corrige a legenda do QR de pareamento no Linux para exibir os mesmos 45 segundos usados pelo timeout real da sessão.
Reduces phone-pairing traffic with 5-second polling and 45-second QR sessions, and adds an explicit retry flow after expiration on Linux and Samsung Tizen.

Reduz o tráfego do pareamento pelo celular com polling a cada 5 segundos e sessões de QR de 45 segundos, além de adicionar uma opção explícita para tentar novamente após a expiração no Linux e Samsung Tizen.

Replaces LAN phone pairing with an encrypted Internet pairing flow backed by a Cloudflare Worker and short-lived Durable Objects. Playlist data is encrypted in the phone browser with AES-256-GCM and decrypted locally by Blazzing.

Substitui o pareamento LAN pelo celular por um fluxo cifrado pela Internet usando Cloudflare Worker e Durable Objects temporários. Os dados da playlist são cifrados no navegador com AES-256-GCM e descriptografados localmente pelo Blazzing.

Fixes phone pairing reachability on LANs by preferring physical Wi-Fi/Ethernet addresses over VPN/container interfaces, using a stable firewall-friendly TCP port when available, and showing the actual port to allow when a host firewall blocks incoming connections.

Adds TV-remote-friendly focus navigation across the home screen, saved playlists, catalog header, search, sidebar and grid, plus phone-assisted M3U/M3U8 entry through a temporary LAN page with a local QR Code and hardened one-time pairing.

Maintenance release based on the finalized v1.3 codebase, with readable/formatted C sources, complete function/prototype comments, refreshed documentation, stale mpv reparenting cleanup and additional static, sanitizer and stress validation.
Introduces the shared Cairo/Pango visual renderer, responsive IPTV cards, modernized hub/login/details/player UI, smooth interaction primitives and a matching Pluto TV redesign.

Fixes M3U routing into TV, movies and series, groups episode entries into series cards with season navigation, strengthens search focus, removes external browser streaming-service entries, and makes player fullscreen reliable under KDE/X11/XWayland.
Redesigns the IPTV and streaming-hub interfaces and adds season-first navigation for series before episode selection.
Hardens thumbnail scheduling, corrupt-artwork handling, mpv IPC and Secret Service writes while prioritizing the active catalog during background prefetch.
Raises the M3U playlist size limit from 32 MiB to 128 MiB for large local and remote playlists, with consistent limit diagnostics.
Automatic provider endpoint discovery after Xtream HTTP 404, with native resolver decoding and verified server failover.
Continuous thumbnail loading with background artwork-only prefetch, bounded FFmpeg frame capture and queue preservation while navigating.
Reliable continuous thumbnail pipeline with bounded queue, fair prefetch and atomic cache writes.
Faster continuous parallel thumbnail loading and background prefetch.
Initial public Blazzing release.
